This appeal is by Respondent No.2/Insurance company challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 29.08.2015, in MVC.No.245/2013 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Shorapur, sitting at Shahapur, whereby the Tribunal granted compensation in a sum of Rs.10,37,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directed appellant - Insurance Company to pay the same.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 06.01.2013, at 10.30 a.m. after purchasing vegetables,
petitioner was returning from B Gudi on his TVS moped bearing registration No.KA-33/H-6426.

While he was near Navodaya School, a Tum-Tum auto bearing registration No.KA-33/4770 (for short 'offending vehicle') came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner from Hothpet side and due to high speed, the driver of the offending vehicle lost control over the vehicle and it dashed against the petitioner.
3.1 In the said accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government General Hospital, Shahapur and after first aid shifted to Vathsalya and Basaveshwara Hospital, Kalaburagi.
Despite treatment, he is not physically impaired.

At the time of accident,
petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was doing agriculture and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
He claimed compensation in a total sum of Rs.10,70,000/- as detailed below:

Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Pain and Suffering 50,000  Loss of income 8,00,000

As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and hence, the petition.
5. Initially the petition was filed by R.Nageshwar Rao seeking compensation in a sum of Rs.10,70,000/- for the personal injury suffered by him in the motor vehicle accident dated 06.01.2013.
During the pendency of the petition, he died and his wife has come on record as his legal representative and prosecuted the petition.

Although, she did not get the claim petition amended, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation by holding that the death of petitioner was on account of the injuries sustained in the said accident.

6. Respondents have appeared through counsel and filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the deceased, nature of injuries suffered and that due to the injury petitioner is physically impaired.
They have also disputed that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Accident was due to the rash or negligent driving by the petitioner himself.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.

6.1 Respondent No.2 has further pleaded that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving license and for violating the terms and conditions of the policy, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

6.2 Since respondent No.2 filed written statement subsequent to the death of petitioner, in the written statement it has further denied that the death of deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
Respondent No.2 has called upon the LR of the petitioner to prove her relationship with the deceased and prays to dismiss the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed issues.
8.

During the enquiry, petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and got Ex.P1 to 12.
9.
On behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Ex.R1 and 2 are marked.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition The Divisional Manager Future General ... vs R Nageshwar Rao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93385978/
3 granting compensation in a sum of Rs.10,37,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.

The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is as under:

 Loss of dependency 6,24,000  Loss of consortium 1,00,000  Funeral expenses 25,000  Transportation charges 10,000  Medical expenses 2,78,483  TOTAL 10,37,483  Rounded of to 10,37,000  11.
Petitioner has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
12. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, respondent No.2 has filed this appeal contending that it is opposed to law, facts and probabilities of the case and as such liable to be set aside.
According to the petitioner, in the alleged accident, he sustained fracture of radius and ulna of the right hand.
The said injuries are not so grievous so as to cause his death.
The medical records does not state that the death of petitioner was on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
The death of petitioner was due to the pre-existing ailments with which he was suffering.
However, the Tribunal has granted compensation as though the death of the petitioner was due to the accidental injuries sustained by him.

12.1 The discharge record of the petitioner given by the Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences,
Hyderabad reveal that petitioner was suffering from hypertension since 10 years, diabetes melatus since 2 years.

sentences.text: He has also undergone Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG).
He has also underwent Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) during 2006.
He was also suffering from Ectopic Left Kidney.
It also states that for fracture of both bones of right forearm, he was operated upon during 2012.
The above and other medical records evidence the fact that petitioner was suffering from hypertension, diabetes and kidney problem.
He also had Brancho Pneumonia.
He died due to all these complications.
Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that immediately after the alleged incident, he underwent treatment.
To make wrongful gain, he has filed claim petition.
12.2 Admittedly, the petitioner was not subjected to post mortem examination to ascertain the cause of death.
The Legal representative of the petitioner has not examined the Doctor who treated the petitioner to prove the cause of death.
In the absence of the same, it cannot be accepted that the death of petitioner was due to the accidental injuries sustained by him.
If there is no nexus between the death and the injury sustained, a petition for compensation is not maintainable.

sentences.text: 16. Heard arguments of both sides and perused the record.

17. Thus, respondent No.2/Insurance company has challenged the impugned judgment and award,
contending that at the outset, petitioner has failed to prove that he sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident and there is no nexus between the alleged accident and the death of the petitioner and consequently, his LR i.e., his wife is not entitled for any compensation.
18. It is relevant to note that the petition came to be filed on 24.08.2013 and petitioner died on 01.06.2014, after lapse of 10 months 8 days.

As already noted, initially the petition was filed by the petitioner claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident and later on during the pendency of the petition, more specifically on 01.06.2014, i.e., after lapse of 10 months,
he died.

Though his wife has came on record as LR of the petitioner, she did not choose to amend the claim petition by pleading that the death of the petitioner was due to the injuries sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident.

Having regard to these aspects, before adverting to the facts of the case and the evidence led by both parties, it is necessary to refer to the two decisions relied upon by learned counsel for appellant i.e., respondent No.2/Insurance Company.

19. In Kannamma, the following question was referred by the Division Bench to the consideration of Full Bench:
The Divisional Manager Future General ... vs R Nageshwar Rao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93385978/
5 "Whether, in a claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, claiming compensation for personal injury resulting from a motor accident as also compensation towards expenses incurred and towards loss of income, etc, if the claimant dies during the pendency of the claim petitioner, his legal representatives can come on record and continue the proceedings ?"

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
( v) A person's claim for compensation for personal injuries under the head loss to his/her estate,
can, on his/her death as a consequence of such injuries, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives, if they do not include a claim for compensation under that head, as and when they file a claim petition under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 110A of the Act, on the death of the person injured."

21. After elaborate discussion, the Hon'ble Division Bench answered the reference as under:
The Divisional Manager Future General ... vs R Nageshwar Rao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93385978/
6

entities.text: Divisional Manager Future General ... vs R Nageshwar Rao And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"(i) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss to estate) cannot, on such person's death occurring not as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained from a motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives; but (ii) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss to estate) can, on such person's death occurring as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives only in so far as the claim for compensation in that claim petition relates to loss to estate of the deceased person due to bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident."
22. Similar question arose for the consideration of the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Uttam Kumar, referred to supra.
Relying upon Kannamma, once again the Hon'ble Full Bench reiterated the said decision.

23. Thus, in the light of the above decisions of the Full Bench of this Hon'ble Court, it is necessary for the LR of the petitioner to prove that the death of petitioner was due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident in question.
In other words, it is for the LR of the petitioner to prove that there is proximity between the accidental injuries sustained and the death of the petitioner.

Even where it is proved that there is casual connection between the injuries suffered and the death, then also the LR of the petitioner can prosecute the claim petition only so far as the claim for compensation relating to the loss to estate of the petitioner due to the bodily injuries sustained in the motor vehicle accident.
Therefore, it is necessary to examine whether the LR of the petitioner is able to establish that the death of the petitioner was due to the accidental injuries suffered by him.
24. It is the definite case of the petitioner that the accident took place on 06.01.2013 and immediately he was taken to government general hospital, Shahapur.
Ex.P-5 is the wound certificate issued by the medical officer, government general hospital, Shahapur, wherein it is stated that the petitioner was brought with the history of road traffic accident.
It is noted that he has suffered three injuries.

Over the page of the said document it is noted that based on the X- ray taken at a private hospital, Gulbarga, it is found that petitioner has suffered fracture of both bones of right forearm and fracture of lateral condyle of right tibia.

However, petitioner has not chosen to produce any document to show that either he took treatment at the government general hospital, Shahapur or at any private hospital at Gulbarga or any other place on 06.01.2013.
25.
The next document relied upon by the petitioner with regard to the treatment in respect of the accidental injuries is Ex.P-11 - the discharge summary issued by Vatsalya Hospital.
From this document it is not possible to ascertain where this hospital is situated.
As per this document petitioner was admitted on 10.01.2013 and discharged on 24.01.2013.

As already noted petitioner The Divisional Manager Future General ... vs R Nageshwar Rao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93385978/
7 has not produced any document to show that from 06.01.2013 to 09.01.2013 he has taken any treatment for the said injuries.

sentences.text: At any stretch of imagination, it cannot be believed that his death was due to the fracture suffered in the accident dated 06.01.2013.
As already discussed, petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that from 06.01.2013 to 09.01.2013, he was under treatment for the fracture suffered in the accident.
As per Ex.P11, on 10.01.2013, he underwent open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with intramedullary nailing, plating with cortical screws on 16.01.2013 under breakchial block.

Neither the petitioner nor his LR are having any explanation as to what treatment he underwent in between 06.01.2013 to 09.01.2013.
33.
In the discharge card at Ex.P9, the words "with fracture of middle third of radius and ulna with implant replaced" are inserted.

However, in the discharge card, there is no reference to petitioner having undergone any operation for implant replacement and there are also no post operative instructions or treatment forthcoming in this document.
In Ex.P10 and the unmarked discharge record of Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad [page No.62 (in red ink)], it is stated that the fractures he suffered are of the year 2012.

34. On 14.07.2022, observing that there is dispute between the parties with regard the nexus between the death and injuries caused in the alleged accident, the following order was passed by this Court referring the matter to the Medical Board, District Hospital, Kalaburagi:
"Released from part heard.
Heard both the counsels.
There is dispute between the parties regarding nexus between the death and injuries caused in the alleged accident.

However, number of voluminous medical records have been produced by the parties and learned counsel for the appellant submitted that all the medical records are nothing to do with the injuries sustained in the accident, but they are pertaining to other regular ailment suffered by the deceased.

Hence, both the counsels submit that all the medical records may be referred to Medical Board to enable the Court to appreciate as to which of the documents are pertaining to the injuries sustained in the accident and to ascertain the real cause of death.
Learned counsel for the appellant also submitted a memo along with questions which are required to be answered by the Medical Board.
Considering the submission made by both the counsels, the matter is referred to the Medical Board of District Hospital, Kalaburagi.

sentences.text: The Medical Board is directed to verify the medical records produced by the claimant and give an opinion regarding the nexus between the injuries suffered in the accident and the cause of death and nexus between the nature of injuries and its impact on the deceased, who was getting treatment for other ailments.
The Medical Board is also directed to give its opinion on questions submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant.

sentences.text: The Registry is directed to send the copies of the medical records to the Medical Board along with the copy of this order.
The Registry is also directed to address a letter to the District Surgeon of District Hospital, Kalaburagi to submit a report within two weeks.
List the matter after three weeks."
35. However, the Medical Board has returned the file stating that "the inpatient case sheets are not produced.
Even though there is discharge summary, they does not contain the complete information.

Since, in-patient records are not produced, it is not possible to give a definite findings as to whether the death of petitioner is due to the injuries sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident".
Thus, based on the material placed on record by the petitioner, the Medical Board is not in a position to give a definite opinion as to the cause of death of the petitioner.

Even otherwise,
from the material on record it is evident the death of the petitioner was due to the severe ailments with which he was suffering and ultimately he suffered cardiac arrest on 06.01.2014.
Absolutely there is no nexus between the injuries suffered by the petitioner and the cause of death.
Consequently, in the light of the decisions of the Full Bench of this Court in Kannamma and Uttam Kumar, the LR of the petitioner is not entitled to continue the case and claim compensation.
Admittedly, the dead body of petitioner is not subjected to post mortem examination.

Consequently,
there is no medical opinion regarding cause of death of the petitioner.
36. As already discussed petitioner filed the claim petition seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

After his death, though his wife has come on record as his LR and continued the petition, she has not at all claimed compensation contending that the death of petitioner was due to the injuries sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident.
She simply continued the claim petition filed by her husband.

Such being the case, without examining whether there was any nexus between the accident and the cause of death, the trial Court has granted the compensation as though it is a petition filed at the first instance for death on account of the accident in question.
37. Moreover, the Medical receipts produced by the petitioner pertains to the treatment taken by him for hypertension, diabetes, heart ailment and kidney problem.
It is doubtful whether he had taken any treatment for the fractures allegedly suffered in the accident dated 06.01.2013.
In fact the very document produced by him state that the fractures were suffered during 2012.

Even where it may be accepted that by mistake instead of 2013, it is noted as 2012, then also it cannot be said that the death of petitioner was on account of the fracture suffered by him in the accident dated 06.01.2013.
38.

In the light of the decisions of the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Kannamma and Uttam Kumar, when LR of petitioner has failed to prove that there is nexus between the death of the petitioner and injuries suffered by him in the alleged accident, she is not entitled to prosecute the petition and claim compensation.
In the light of the above facts, the decisions in Somavva, Hema and Oriental referred to supra and relied upon by the LR of petitioner are not applicable to the case on hand.

While he was near Navodaya School, a Tum-Tum auto bearing registration No.KA-33/4770 (for short 'offending vehicle') came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner from Hothpet side and due to high speed, the driver of the offending vehicle lost control over the vehicle and it dashed against the petitioner.
The death of petitioner was due to the pre-existing ailments with which he was suffering.
He died due to all these complications.
Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that immediately after the alleged incident, he underwent treatment.
To make wrongful gain, he has filed claim petition.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
12.2 Admittedly, the petitioner was not subjected to post mortem examination to ascertain the cause of death.
The Legal representative of the petitioner has not examined the Doctor who treated the petitioner to prove the cause of death.
In the absence of the same, it cannot be accepted that the death of petitioner was due to the accidental injuries sustained by him.
If there is no nexus between the death and the injury sustained, a petition for compensation is not maintainable.
In support of her arguments, learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company has relied upon the following decisions:
(i) Uttam Kumar (Decd) Vs. Madhav and Anr.
(Uttam Kumar)1 (ii) Kannamma Vs. Deputy General Manager (Kannamma)2 14.
15. Learned counsel appearing for respondent has relied upon the following decisions:
(i) Smt.Somavva and Ors Vs. Vijayakumar and Ors.
(Smt.Somavva)3 (ii) Smt.Hema and Ors. Vs.Smt.Santhoshi Shivaji Deshmukh & Anr.
(Smt.Hema)4 (iii) The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon (Decd) through his Legal Representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan & Anr. Oriental)5 2002 (3) Kar.L.J.337(FB) ILR 1990 KAR 4300 2010 Kant MAC 557 (Kant)
17. Thus, respondent No.2/Insurance company has challenged the impugned judgment and award,
contending that at the outset, petitioner has failed to prove that he sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident and there is no nexus between the alleged accident and the death of the petitioner and consequently, his LR i.e., his wife is not entitled for any compensation.
18. It is relevant to note that the petition came to be filed on 24.08.2013 and petitioner died on 01.06.2014, after lapse of 10 months 8 days.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
"(i) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss to estate) cannot, on such person's death occurring not as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained from a motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives; but (ii) A claim petition presented under Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by the person sustaining bodily injuries in a motor accident, claiming compensation for personal injuries as also for compensation towards expenses, loss of income, etc.,
(loss to estate) can, on such person's death occurring as a result or consequence of bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident, be prosecuted by his/her legal representatives only in so far as the claim for compensation in that claim petition relates to loss to estate of the deceased person due to bodily injuries sustained in the motor accident."
22. Similar question arose for the consideration of the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Uttam Kumar, referred to supra.
In other words, it is for the LR of the petitioner to prove that there is proximity between the accidental injuries sustained and the death of the petitioner.
Even where it is proved that there is casual connection between the injuries suffered and the death, then also the LR of the petitioner can prosecute the claim petition only so far as the claim for compensation relating to the loss to estate of the petitioner due to the bodily injuries sustained in the motor vehicle accident.
Thus, based on the material placed on record by the petitioner, the Medical Board is not in a position to give a definite opinion as to the cause of death of the petitioner.
Even otherwise,
from the material on record it is evident the death of the petitioner was due to the severe ailments with which he was suffering and ultimately he suffered cardiac arrest on 06.01.2014.
Absolutely there is no nexus between the injuries suffered by the petitioner and the cause of death.
Admittedly, the dead body of petitioner is not subjected to post mortem examination.
Consequently,
there is no medical opinion regarding cause of death of the petitioner.
After his death, though his wife has come on record as his LR and continued the petition, she has not at all claimed compensation contending that the death of petitioner was due to the injuries sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident.
She simply continued the claim petition filed by her husband.
Such being the case, without examining whether there was any nexus between the accident and the cause of death, the trial Court has granted the compensation as though it is a petition filed at the first instance for death on account of the accident in question.
Even where it may be accepted that by mistake instead of 2013, it is noted as 2012, then also it cannot be said that the death of petitioner was on account of the fracture suffered by him in the accident dated 06.01.2013.
38.
In the light of the decisions of the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Kannamma and Uttam Kumar, when LR of petitioner has failed to prove that there is nexus between the death of the petitioner and injuries suffered by him in the alleged accident, she is not entitled to prosecute the petition and claim compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the light of the above facts, the decisions in Somavva, Hema and Oriental referred to supra and relied upon by the LR of petitioner are not applicable to the case on hand.
In the result, the appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal filed by respondent No.2/Insurance Company is allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 29.08.2015 in MVC.No.245/2013 is set aside and consequently it is dismissed.
(iii) The appellant/respondent No.2 is at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit (if any).
 (iv) The registry is directed to send back the trial  Court record along with copy of this  judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
